rationale: Internally consistent and the burn-rate denominator (dlc + R&D spend) is a defensible twist on the runway idea, but it sits close to the already-tested che/lct and cash-to-liability coverage legs in the archive, so expect substantial overlap rather than fresh information.

This is essentially the sign-flipped "Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor" (TS_MIN → NEG TS_RANK of oancf/at) bolted onto the debt leg from the already-failed "R&D Cash-Flow Volatility Debt Trap," making it a cosmetic recombination of two archived signals rather than a new mechanism.

Substituting second-moment stability for the archived level-based "R&D Working-Capital Normalization" is a genuine change in signal content, though the low-fundamental-volatility leg risks proxying the known earnings/cash-flow volatility anomaly and size, so any alpha should be checked against those controls.

This is the archived "Goodwill Equity-Cushion Cash Burn" with ceq replaced by ABS(ceq) — a one-function robustness tweak affecting only the small negative-equity tail, not a substantively different signal.

The impairment-plus-refinancing story is coherent and the margin-erosion leg is a real departure from the archive's liquidity/net-debt goodwill conditioners, though it remains a mashup of previously used components and the leverage leg will largely reproduce the earlier goodwill-leverage results.

Cash taxes are a genuinely different, harder-to-manipulate validation channel than the archive's gross-surplus, accrual, and cash-flow addback legs, but txt/lt is close enough to a scaled profitability ratio that FF5's RMW may absorb much of the alpha, so the marginal contribution over "R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover" is the key thing to measure.
